claims.statement: The fragment introduces assignment status changes as prevention of acceptance/submission, then explicitly states Active permits invitation-link acceptance and Inactive invalidates that link. Link invalidation alone does not prove existing repository write access is revoked; actual submission enforcement and accepted-student paths require separate behavior evidence.

The assignment title is entered explicitly and its prefix can optionally be edited via a pencil control. These mutable labels are not durable identity, a naming-policy mandate or proof of a created repository.

The classroom-admin fragment only points to the management article's administration section. It supplies no role permissions itself and does not inherit full review of that parent or grant admin authority.

When applicable, a CLI subcommand prompts for classroom selection. Applicability is conditional; interactive selection does not establish tenant identity, authorization or successful subcommand execution, and the fragment specifies no command.

Codespaces is an optional assignment environment offering browser-based VS Code with one-click setup. The source capability does not prove provisioning, safe code, zero cost, available capacity or consent to run billable environments; linked details remain separate evidence.

Group assignments create a single shared team repository owned by the teacher's organization account, not by an individual student. It may be empty or generated from starter templates containing code, docs, tests and resources; access is granted to student-created/joined teams at acceptance. Source access semantics do not certify actual membership, effective permissions, template safety or licensing.
